but when buoyancy exerts an upwards and downwards force, what need for gravity is there?

Buoyancy isn't an upward force, or any force at all.

Gravity is can be measured with this formula: F = (G * (m1 * m2) / d^2

  • F (Force in Newtons)
  • G (Gravitational Constant) 6.67x10*-11
  • m1 (mass of Earth in Kg)
  • m2 (mass of whatever you are measuring the force of gravity on in Kg)
  • d = distance between the two masses.

Short version: Given any two objects, the one with less mass will be effected very slightly less by Earth's gravity than the more massive object. Since the overall mass of a volume of oil is less than the overall mass of a volume of water, the oil will float on water because the effect of gravity on it is slightly less the the effect on water. Hence, buoyancy is not a force.
